questions.stem: Which of the following statement are not related to the pathogenesis of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis

options.label: C
options.text: Loss of function mutation in TERT and TERC gene

options.label: D
options.text: Mutations in genes encoding components of surfactant

questions.solutionHtml:
Age less than 20 years

IPF is a disease of older individuals, rarely appearing before the age of 50 years.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 507

questions.stem: All of the following statements are true regarding idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis except:

options.label: A
options.text: Plural surfaces are cobblestone in appearance

options.label: B
options.text: White areas of fibrosis in the lower lobes

options.label: D
options.text: All fibrotic lesions are of the same age

questions.answerText: All fibrotic lesions are of the same age
questions.solutionHtml:
All fibrotic lesions are of the same age
  • The fibrotic lesions in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis are not of the same age.
  • They show spatial heterogeneity (I.e patchy lesion distribution) and temporal heterogeneity (i.e lesions of different ages side-by-side)


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 507

questions.stemHtml: The lung biopsy of a 50-year-old patient is shown below based on the histopathological findings. What is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
UIP

The given histopathological picture showing patchy interstitial fibrosis, showing a honeycomb appearance is suggestive of Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP).



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 508,509

questions.stem: Which of the following histopathological findings is typically seen in non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP)?

options.label: A
options.text: Honeycomb cysts with peripheral subpleural distribution

options.label: B
options.text: Homogeneous interstitial infiltrate of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and macrophages

options.label: C
options.text: Granulomatous inflammation with non-caseating epithelioid cell granulomas

options.label: D
options.text: Diffuse alveolar damage with hyaline membrane formation

questions.answerText: Homogeneous interstitial infiltrate of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and macrophages
questions.solutionHtml:
Homogeneous interstitial infiltrate of lymphocytes, plasma cells, and macrophages
  • Non-specific interstitial pneumonia (NSIP) is a form of interstitial lung disease characterized by inflammation and fibrosis within the lung tissue.
  • The cellular patternconsists primarily of mild to moderate chronic interstitial inflammation, containing lymphocytes and a few plasma cells, in auniform or patchy distribution.


Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 507,508

questions.stemHtml: A 40-year-old patient presented with complaints of cough and dyspnoea and a chest x-ray demonstrate patchy areas of consolidation. A histopathological examination is shown below. Based on the findings, what is your diagnosis?
questions.solutionHtml:
Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia

The given clinical scenario with the patient's clinical presentation of cough and dyspnea with patchy areas of consolidation on chest x-ray, and histopathological image showing Masson bodies is suggestive of Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia.



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 507,508

questions.stem: A 60-year-old patient with a history of sepsis now presents with persistent hypoxemia. A diagnosis of ARDS is made. All of the following statements are true regarding histological features of an ARDS except

options.label: C
options.text: Alveolar walls are lined by a hyaline membrane

questions.solutionHtml:
Type I pneumocyte hyperplasia

Type II pneumocyte hyperplasia is a common finding in ARDS due to the need for regeneration of the damaged type I pneumocytes



Robbins & Cotran Pathologic Basis of Disease, 10th Edition, Page No. 496,497
